question: ₹2,500, when invested for 8 years at a given rate of simple interest per year, amounted to ₹3,725 on maturity. What was the rate of simple interest that was paid per annum?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simple Interest for 8 years = 3725 − 2500 = 1225

Interest for 1 year = 1225 ÷ 8 = 153.125

Rate % = (153.125 ÷ 2500) × 100 = 6.125%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.125%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2500

Amount (A) = ₹3725

Time (T) = 8 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = A − P

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
• T = 0 Years P = ₹2500 T = 8 Years A = ₹3725 
 
 SI = ₹1225 Rate = R% 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = 3725 − 2500 = 1225

⇒ 1225 = (2500 × R × 8) ÷ 100

⇒ 1225 = 200 × R

⇒ R = 1225 ÷ 200

⇒ R = 6.125%

**∴ The correct answer is 6.125%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum Becoming 'n' Times at SI

When a certain sum of money becomes 'n' times of itself in 'T' years at Simple Interest, the rate of interest is given by R = 100 × (n − 1) ÷ T.

Compound Interest Formula

Amount under Compound Interest is calculated as A = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T, where interest is compounded annually.

Difference Between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest is calculated directly using the formula D = P × (R ÷ 100)².
